summary: The proposal has a defined problem, objectives, architecture, and implementation direction, but it is not ready for submission. The missing Abstract and AI-review confirmation are important completeness issues, while the Problem section, introductory structure, and Objective 2 require substantive revision; several minor wording and figure-caption improvements are also needed.

findings.title: Missing Abstract
findings.description: Add an Abstract of approximately one-third to one-half page summarizing the problem, motivation, objectives, and proposed approach.

findings.title: Missing confirmation of review of AI-generated text
findings.description: Add an explicit first-person sentence confirming that you carefully checked all text generated with the AI tool for correctness and coherence, as required by the transparency guidelines.

locations.quote: I used the following generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool while preparing this proposal.

findings.title: Problem section presents workarounds and a proposed solution
findings.description: Revise the Problem section so that it describes only the problems and their negative consequences. Remove solution-oriented statements and rewrite workaround descriptions solely in terms of their effects on affected actors.

locations.quote: The usual workaround hands the maintainer full administrative rights over every user and every host.
**A self-service platform that arms the workflow engine of Keycloak with an expiry date at grant time would end this accumulation.**

findings.title: Missing introductory text before subsection 1.1
findings.description: Add a brief introductory paragraph at the beginning of Section 1 before subsection 1.1. The paragraph should preview the Introduction's coverage of the context, infrastructure, and transition to the problem statement.

findings.title: Objective 2 contains double verbs
findings.description: Use one primary action verb for Objective 2 rather than the coordinated verbs “Design” and “implement.” For example, replace it with “Implement connectors with expiry,” and apply the same change to the corresponding subsection heading.

locations.section: 4.2 Design and Implement Connectors with Expiry

findings.title: Inconsistent naming for the request-review role
findings.description: Use one term consistently for the request-review role, or explicitly define the distinction between “maintainer” and “resource owner.”

locations.quote: **Maintainers**, the staf who look after a project, know whether a request is legitimate but lack the rights to act on it, while the super admin holds the rights but lacks the context.

locations.section: Delegate Request Review Without Privilege Escalation
locations.quote: Keycloak requires a realm-wide administrative role for its workfow API, and **no resource owner** may hold that role.

locations.section: Delegate Request Review Without Privilege Escalation
locations.quote: The **resource owner** completes a request alone when it touches only non-privileged bindings, such as a Slack channel.

findings.title: Figure 2 has an uninformative caption
findings.description: Replace the generic caption with a descriptive caption identifying the main platform components, external systems, interfaces, and the depicted grant, provisioning, and deprovisioning flows.

locations.section: Objective — Design and Implement Connectors with Expiry

findings.title: Contraction used
findings.description: Replace the contraction “doesn’t” with the full form “does not.”

locations.quote: The current process **doesn’t** scale and is the worst bottleneck of the chair.
